question.problem:
A drone has a $65%$ chance of successfully delivering a package. It makes $5$ deliveries in one day. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, what is the probability that it succeeds at most $3$ times?

Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of successful deliveries.

Here, we have the following information:

- There are $n=5$ deliveries.

- The probability of success is $p=65%=0.65.$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(5,0.65).$

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for the probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{x})(0.65)^{x}(1-0.65)^{5-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{x})(0.65)^{x}(0.35)^{5-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability that the drone succeeds at most $3$ times. This corresponds to $P(X\le 3).$

However, computing

$$
P(X\le 3)=P(X=0)+P(X=1)+…+P(X=3),
$$

will involve many computations, so let's express our answer in terms of the complement instead. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =1-P(X>3) \\  & =1-[P(X=4)+P(X=5)] \\  & =1-[(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{4})(0.65)^{4}(0.35)^{5-4}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{5})(0.65)^{5}(0.35)^{5-5}] \\  & =1-[5(0.65)^{4}(0.35)+(0.65)^{5}] \\  & =1-0.428\,415 \\  & ≈0.572,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
